Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for the chase. Temba Bavuma leads his troops out on the park. It will be the left-hand, right-hand combination of Yashasvi Jaiswal and Rohit Sharma to open the innings for India. Marco Jansen will kickstart proceedings. Jansen to Jaiswal. Two slips await. Here we go!
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, India will back themselves to chase down this total, but they will need to be cautious early on with the ball expected to move around a bit under the lights. As for the dew, based on what KL Rahul mentioned during the toss, it is not expected to be as prominent as it was in Ranchi or Raipur. Kuldeep Yadav also shared that the old ball held in the surface, and if that continues into the second innings and the dew does not arrive, stroke-making may not be straightforward. All in all, an intriguing chase awaits. Back in a bit for India's reply.

Kuldeep Yadav is up for a quick chat. He starts by saying that the pacers Harshit and Arshdeep started off well for them as they bowled on tight lines and lengths in the Powerplay. Highlights that it was gripping when the spinners came in. Adds that he tried to mix up the pace. Details that bowling with a dry ball has been a luxury after the first two games. Says they lost 20 successive tosses, but they won this time and expresses his happiness about that. On the appeals and requests for reviews, he admits that he is someone who is not spot on with the reviews. Shares that Rohit keeps pulling his leg whenever he is bowling or appealing. Mentions that he tries to hit the pads and if he succeeds in doing so, he feels that every ball is a wicket. Says that you need seniors like the former captain Rohit Sharma to guide you, and also appreciates KL Rahul by saying that KL has been brilliant behind the stumps. On being asked about how the wicket is playing, Kuldeep mentions it is still a good surface to bat on. Also points out that because of the 34-over ball change rule, the ball was dry and was holding well onto the pitch. Also says that it wasn't that easy to score runs when the ball turned. Ends by saying he tried a lot of variations like the conventional leggie, the googly and the flipper to trap the batters.

KL Rahul dangled the carrot by introducing Kuldeep Yadav, and neither Dewald Brevis nor Marco Jansen could resist. Both departed in the same over to the left-arm wrist spinner that came as a bruising double blow for the tourists. From there, Kuldeep proved far too good for the rest of the lower order, and Prasidh Krishna stepped in to complete the cleanup job.

However, the momentum shifted quickly when Prasidh Krishna’s first two overs went for 27 runs, allowing de Kock to break free while Bavuma, though less fluent, kept ticking along. Krishna, though, redeemed himself on his return to the attack by striking twice in an over. That shifted the tide decisively, as South Africa had been progressing comfortably until that point. De Kock went on to bring up his 23rd ODI hundred but fell soon after. At 199/5 with about 17 overs remaining and not a lot of batting to come, Dewald Brevis and Marco Jansen needed to decide whether to go hard or lay a platform by keeping wickets in hand.

Earlier, India finally ended their streak of 20 consecutive toss losses in ODIs and opted to bowl first. South Africa made a tweak at the top, with Aiden Markram, fresh off a match-winning century in Raipur, moving down the order. Ryan Rickelton opened with Quinton de Kock, but his stay was short-lived as he fell for his second duck of the series in the very first over. Arshdeep Singh and Harshit Rana made good use of the new ball on a surface that offered noticeable spongy bounce early on. There was just enough movement in the air and off the pitch to keep Temba Bavuma and Quinton de Kock uncertain, resulting in a cautious start.

A job well done by India. While 270 is a competitive total, the Proteas looked on course for much more at the halfway mark. After letting themselves down with both the ball and in the field in Raipur, the dry conditions here certainly helped the home side, and Kuldeep Yadav in particular made the most of what was on offer.

Commentary.Commentary: All in readiness for the decider to get underway. Nearly a full house already, and it will not be long before every seat is taken. The two umpires make their way out to the middle, followed by KL Rahul and his men. A surprise at the top of the order as Aiden Markram is not opening for the Proteas. It will be Ryan Rickelton to open the innings alongside Quinton de Kock. Arshdeep Singh will bowl the first over. Arshdeep to de Kock. Two slips in place. Let's go...

The captain of South Africa, Temba Bavuma says that he would have bowled first as well. Tells that it is now about getting off to a good start and setting it up for the middle order. Adds that the previous encounters were entertaining, and once again, it is a packed crowd. Informs that Tony de Zorzi and Nandre Burger miss out due to injuries, and he expects them to be out for a couple of weeks. Adds that Ryan Rickelton and Ottneil Baartman come back into the side.

KL Rahul, the Indian captain, says that they will bowl first because of the dew and adds that they trained here last evening, where the dew came in a bit later than in Ranchi and Raipur. Reckons that the surface looks good and adds that they are happy with the cricket they have played so far, even after failing to defend 360 runs, but that was more due to the conditions, and they are just looking to tweak a few little things here and there. Informs that they have one change with Tilak Varma coming in for Washington Sundar.

South Africa (Playing XI) - Aiden Markram, Quinton de Kock (WK), Ryan Rickelton (In for Tony de Zorzi), Temba Bavuma (C), Matthew Breetzke, Dewald Brevis, Marco Jansen, Corbin Bosch, Keshav Maharaj, Lungi Ngidi, Ottneil Baartman (In for Nandre Burger).

India (Playing XI) - Yashasvi Jaiswal, Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli, Ruturaj Gaikwad, Tilak Varma (In for Washington Sundar), KL Rahul (C/WK), Ravindra Jadeja, Harshit Rana, Arshdeep Singh, Kuldeep Yadav, Prasidh Krishna.
TOSS - KL Rahul flips the coin with his left hand, and it works for him. India have won the toss and they will BOWL first.

PITCH REPORT - Deep Dasgupta notes that it is a warm afternoon in Vizag and points out the boundary dimensions with boundaries measuring 63 and 62 metres square of the wicket and the straight boundary at 73 metres. Shaun Pollock adds that the wicket is nice and hard, and he expects another high-scoring game. Mentions there is a good grass covering that should keep the surface intact, and although there are a few cracks, he does not expect them to play any significant role. Feels that the captain winning the toss will once again prefer chasing. Deep shares that there was no noticeable dew around 8 pm local time yesterday, which will be some consolation for the team bowling second. He describes the surface as a mix of red and black soil, roughly a 70-30 combination, which should provide good bounce and carry. Reckons that if there is anything in it for the spinners, it is likely to come in the first half of the match, and the surface may play a little slower during the day.

Dew has had a major say in the two games so far, with batting under lights being easier, and that should be the case today as well. India have lost the flip of the coin for 20 ODIs in a row, with their last toss win coming in the 2023 ODI World Cup semifinal against New Zealand. The first two games have been quite the ride with the pendulum swinging back and forth. Let's hope we are treated to another entertaining game. Stick around for the toss and team news.

South Africa, meanwhile, showed tremendous character under pressure in the second ODI. Aiden Markram led the chase with a brilliant hundred, anchoring the innings and guiding his side to a famous win. Vital knocks from Matthew Breetzke, Dewald Brevis and skipper Temba Bavuma ably supported him. Tony de Zorzi and Nandre Burger went down with hamstring discomfort in the last game and have been ruled out of the decider, which is a blow for the Proteas.

India come into this match with a batting lineup brimming with confidence. In the previous game, Virat Kohli made it back-to-back tons while Ruturaj Gaikwad notched up his maiden ODI century. Despite the late flourish from KL Rahul, the hosts could not provide the cushion for the bowlers in dewy conditions, something they will want to correct if they bat first again today. With the ball and in the field, India left much to be desired and will look to execute better.

A very warm welcome to one and all, joining us for the finale in this three-match ODI series as India take on South Africa at the Dr. Y.S. Rajasekhara Reddy ACA-VDCA Cricket Stadium in Vizag. It was a riveting second game in Raipur, where India piled up 358, but the Proteas chased it down with four balls to spare, and now the series stands deadlocked at 1-1.

The stage is set for a thrilling finale as India lock horns with South Africa in the third and final One Day International, a winner-takes-all series decider at the Dr. Y.S. Rajasekhara Reddy ACA-VDCA Cricket Stadium in Visakhapatnam. With the series perfectly poised at 1-1, after two high-scoring and intensely fought contests, the pressure is immense on both the stand-in Indian skipper, KL Rahul and his Proteas counterpart, Temba Bavuma, to lead their sides to victory. Both matches have been a feast for the batters, with the pitches and the ever-present factor of dew making life extremely difficult for the bowlers in the second innings. India's batting lineup has been phenomenal, with Virat Kohli continuing his incredible form by smashing back-to-back centuries. Ruturaj Gaikwad's maiden ODI ton in the second match provides a massive boost, complementing the aggressive starts provided by Rohit Sharma and Yashasvi Jaiswal, and the explosive finishing of KL Rahul. The fast bowlers, particularly Prasidh Krishna, have been expensive and lack control in the late overs. The team's inability to defend a score of 358 highlights a tactical and execution problem, especially in the dew-affected second innings. On the other hand, South Africa have rebounded strongly from their first ODI loss, carrying all the momentum into the decider. Their batting depth and fearlessness in the chase were the main takeaways from the second ODI. The Proteas attack, led by the left-arm pacer Marco Jansen, has looked good in patches and the return of the likes of Lungi Ngidi and Keshav Maharaj in the 2nd ODI was somewhat positive. However, they now have a couple of injury concerns as Nandre Burger and Tony de Zorzi both seemed to suffer hamstring injuries. This decider is a battle between India's superstar top-order and South Africa's relentless batting depth. The result is likely to hinge on which team adapts better to the conditions, especially in managing the wet ball. Given the trend of chasing teams having a significant advantage in the series, the toss will undoubtedly be a crucial factor. Who are you backing for the win?
